pl-l4d22c1-d1e115.summary: Asks, since many authorities hold that sins are forgiven in true contrition before confession or satisfaction, even to one who will later relapse, whether forgiven sins return if, after contrition, he scorns confession or falls back into the same or similar sin.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e118.summary: Notes that the solution is obscure and complex, some asserting and others denying that sins once forgiven are later brought back for punishment.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e121.summary: Notes that those who say forgiven sins return support themselves with the following testimonies.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e125.summary: Quotes Ambrose: forgive one another; otherwise God demands back what was forgiven; if they are scorned, he will revoke the sentence by which he gave mercy, as with the wicked servant in the Gospel.
claims: God revokes forgiveness from the unforgiving.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e134.summary: Quotes Rabanus: God handed the wicked servant to the torturers until he paid the whole debt, since not only post-baptismal sins but also original sins forgiven in baptism will be counted against him.
claims: Even sins forgiven in baptism are counted against the unforgiving.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e142.summary: Quotes Gregory: the Gospel shows that if we do not forgive from the heart, what we rejoiced was forgiven us through penance is demanded again.
claims: Forgiveness is demanded back from the unforgiving.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e151.summary: Quotes Augustine: God says, forgive and you will be forgiven; I forgave first, forgive at least afterward; if you do not, I will recall you and bring back all I forgave.
claims: God brings back forgiven sins to the unforgiving.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e163.summary: Adds: whoever, forgetting God's benefit, wants to avenge his injuries will not only merit no pardon for future sins but will have past sins, which he thought forgiven, brought back for punishment.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e169.summary: Quotes Bede on 'I will return to my house': this verse is to be feared, not explained, lest a fault we thought extinguished overwhelm us through negligence.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e182.summary: Adds: whomever heresy or worldly desire seizes after baptism, it soon casts down into the depths of all vices.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e188.summary: Quotes Augustine: the Lord most clearly teaches in the Gospel that forgiven sins return where there is no fraternal charity, in the servant from whom the forgiven debt was demanded because he would not forgive his fellow servant.
claims: Forgiven sins return without fraternal charity.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e197.summary: Notes that on these authorities rest those who say forgiven sins return if repeated.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e200.summary: Gives the objection: if someone is punished again for a sin he repented of and was forgiven, it seems unjust; if punished for what he did not amend, the justice is plain; if what was forgiven is demanded, it is either injustice or hidden justice. God would seem to judge twice, against Scripture.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e209.summary: Answers for the first view that there is neither double tribulation nor double judgment, which would happen only if God punished again after worthy satisfaction; but one who did not persevere did not satisfy worthily. He should have remembered his sin continually, to avoid it, and God's benefits, as many as his forgiven sins, giving thanks to the end; but returning ungrateful like a dog to its vomit, he killed his past goods and recalled his forgiven sin, so God imputes to him, proud and ungrateful, what he forgave him when humble.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e218.summary: Gives the second view: since it seems absurd that forgiven sins be imputed again, some hold that no one is punished again by God for sins once forgiven, but forgiven sins are said to return because through ingratitude one becomes as guilty and sinful as before.
claims: Forgiven sins are not punished again; ingratitude makes one equally guilty.

pl-l4d22c1-d1e222.summary: Concludes that approved doctors favor both sides, so without prejudging either he leaves the judgment to the studious reader, adding that it seems safe and near salvation to eat crumbs under the masters' table.
claims: Lombard leaves the question of returning sins undecided.

pl-l4d22c1.summary: Asks whether sins forgiven through contrition return if one later scorns confession or falls into the same or similar sin. The question is obscure. Those who say they return cite Ambrose, Rabanus, Gregory, Augustine, and Bede on the unforgiving servant, whose forgiven debt was demanded again. Against them it seems unjust to punish forgiven sin, and God does not judge twice; they answer that it is not double punishment, since one who did not persevere did not satisfy sufficiently, and ingratitude revives forgiven sin. Others say no one is punished again for forgiven sins, but ingratitude makes one as guilty as before. Since approved doctors favor both, Lombard leaves the judgment to the reader, content to eat crumbs beneath the masters' table.
claims: Whether forgiven sins return upon relapse is disputed.
Some hold forgiven sins return through ingratitude, as with the unforgiving servant.
Others hold forgiven sins are not punished again but ingratitude makes one as guilty.
